goal: Prepare a source-bound historical and technical learning card for the 1954 Fender Stratocaster, separating original design from later model variants.

source_documents.locator: History of the Fender Stratocaster: The 1950s, development and design sections
facts: Stratocaster appeared in 1954 after development involving Leo Fender and colleagues, including Freddy Tavares, Don Randall and musician feedback such as Rex Gallion.

Early design had a contoured solid body, three single-coil pickups, a three-position selector, master volume and two tone controls for neck and middle pickups; the original bridge pickup had no separate tone control.
The revised vibrato bridge moves the bridge assembly with strings, uses a rear spring cavity and an arm to vary pitch; Fender historically called it tremolo.
The original selector provided three pickup choices, not the later standard five-position combinations.
Fender dates the Stratocaster's introduction to 1954 and marked its 70th anniversary in 2024.
The 2024 anniversary announcement describes multiple modern Stratocaster models with different necks and pickups; one historic specification must not be generalized to every Stratocaster.
